title: You Have Some Homework To Do To Make The Most Of Star Wars Zero Company
description: Star Wars Zero Company takes place right at the end of The Clone Wars, my favorite period in Star Wars' huge timeline. That conflict begins with the Battle of Geonosis in Attack of the Clones and concludes with the deaths of the Separatist leaders in Revenge of the Sith, but a vast majority of the galaxy-spanning war is covered in the seven seasons of Star Wars: The Clone Wars. As such, Zero Company makes several references to the earlier seasons of the TV show that debuted in 2008. The biggest one, of what I've seen of the game so far anyway, comes right at the start of the story: Protagonist Hawks was made the scapegoat for a battle that went very wrong while working under General Pong Krell. And, man, that name does a tremendous amount of narrative heavy lifting in characterizing Hawks. With one name, Bit Reactor basically gave me all the proof I needed that Hawks had not only seen some truly horrendous war crimes, but that whatever they were accused of was almost certainly not true. "The intended effect of the line worked, then," Bit Reactor narrative director Aaron Contreras told me. "Like, [Republic Intelligence] is talking about whether they can trust this guy, because he's a washout and a loser--he worked for Pong Krell. And so every [player] who knows this guy is like, 'It's not [Hawks'] fault then. That's the worst boss ever." So even if you don't need to know Pong Krell to play Zero Company, I highly recommend you familiarize yourself with him beforehand. And the best way to do that is by watching The Clone Wars. Or, at the very least, one specific arc: Season 4's four-episode Umbara Arc. The Clone Wars is always a tough show for me to recommend because it has some absolutely stellar episodes of television hidden in between mind-numbing episodes that are too silly or simply excruciatingly dull. I can only see Jar Jar Binks on my screen for so many minutes before I contemplate punching my TV. But the show's gems are really, really good, largely for how…

title: Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls Is Making The Wait For Injustice 3 Much More Bearable
description: Let me get this straight: I play a lot of the best fighting games. I enjoy playing them. I am not good at the genre. Anything online requires me to adapt to players far beyond my skill level, and it’s almost pointless for me to attempt to reach that level. I just don’t have the time or patience to do it, but that doesn’t mean I can’t praise a game when it smashes it out of the park. After waiting for almost a decade for Injustice 3, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is keeping me occupied, and, to be honest, it may even be better than NetherRealm Studios’ take. While they share the same core DNA, they’re fairly different takes on fighting games. Marvel Tokon is a tag-team-centric fighter, similar to Arc System Works’ Dragon Ball FighterZ, while Injustice 2 takes the familiar one-on-one approach that games like Mortal Kombat deliver. Same genre, different niche, and while I typically prefer the style that NetherRealm offers, Marvel Tokon has turned me into a tag-fighter player. Playing as the various Marvel superheroes, each with a distinct style developed by Arc System Works, makes every match feel distinct. While the story modes are essentially fights with various teams, interspersed with cinematic and comic book-style storytelling, they do a good job of teaching you the game’s mechanics. I do prefer the Injustice or Mortal Kombat style of fighting game stories, but this gives you a way to play with all of the teams in the game. However, I have spent most of my time (see: a ridiculous amount) playing the Arcadia Rumble mode. In it, you pick your characters, customize your avatar (I have an Anti-Venom-style Spider-Man holding Captain America’s Shield and Deadpool’s Katana), and compete against other players to collect shards and level up your perks. There are also Mario Kart-style power-ups that can unleash attacks on other players, earning you stars that you need to win. Each avatar-led round concludes with a fighting session, where you can earn more stars based on the…

title: Starfield Discount Drops The Sci-Fi RPG To Its Lowest Price Yet
description: As someone who talks about their fascination with space to an unhealthy degree, you can bet that Starfield was my most anticipated game for years. The first original IP from Bethesda Game Studios in over two decades, it looked like a sci-fi take on Fallout, offering a new universe to explore from the developer behind some of the best RPGs available. While it initially didn’t live up to my hefty expectations, it’s now in better shape following multiple updates. Best of all, you can get it even cheaper than I did, as the game is at its lowest price ever right now. If you’re even somewhat interested in travelling to space (hello, No Man’s Sky players), I shouldn’t need to sell you on Starfield. The story sends you on a planet-hopping adventure through the stars, seeing you hunt for the meaning of the universe. Yes, the one we currently reside in. That means working with Constellation, a crew of people looking to find the meaning of life (not 42) and mysterious artifacts that will help you find that exact answer. Of course, in familiar Bethesda RPG fashion, the main narrative rarely remains the focal point. As you meet a range of characters, fight with other factions, or simply go hunting for treasure, you’ll find yourself off the beaten track far more than you expect. Every side quest starts as, "I’ll just take a quick trip to this planet," and suddenly, you’ve started an entirely new secondary plot. Constellation can wait. It also differentiates itself from the two elephants in the room-Fallout and The Elder Scrolls-with relative success. Sure, the gunplay will be familiar to long-term Vault Dwellers, which isn’t surprising considering that it shares the same developer, but the vibes are different. And after an initial playthrough, the mod selection is hefty, to say the least. There’s a modpack that basically converts Starfield into Star Wars. Obviously, the right way to play is always a vanilla run first, but the options for changing the game are endless. There are…

title: Rideshare Stimulator Outlines AI Usage After Contentious Exchange With Ex-Writer
description: After Saber Interactive unveiled its upcoming title Rideshare Stimulater, former lead writer Stella Sacco came forward and said that she had been replaced by ChatGPT during development. Saber CEO Matthew Karch denied Sacco's allegation that she had been replaced by AI, but the company has now shared previously undisclosed details about Rideshare Stimulator's AI usage. Rideshare Stimulator casts players as a driver who can pick up a seemingly infinite number of passengers and interact with them while getting them to their final destinations. According to the new disclosure on the game's Steam page, Rideshare Stimulator uses AI tools for "voice generation and some localization" and AI-generated passenger missions that can be skipped if players only want "human-written narrative content." It also adds that the game will have radio stations with "human-made music and AI-generated music," with the latter being clearly labeled in-game. However, Saber flatly states that "the main campaign story, characters, and dialogue are written by a team of human writers." Earlier this week, Sacco said that she was replaced as the game's lead writer by AI "midway through development." "They took me off the project to use ChatGPT to write the rest of the text, including planned live updates," Sacco told PC Gamer in a subsequent statement. "If they changed plans in the intervening years, that's great. But again: I was there, and it was my job to write the game, and then it wasn't once Matt Karch decided using ChatGPT would be great publicity for the game." Karch released a statement of his own with This Week in Videogames that added greater controversy to the story by claiming that Stella "violated" her agreement with the company. "Stella who? I had to ask Claude because I have never spoken to her or seen her. We have already said we are using AI for certain parts of the game and will update the Steam page once we have finalized the feature set. Let me clarify that the entire story…
